paragraphs: I did a one-month clerkship at Korea University in Seoul, South Korea. I feel I had a truly irreplaceable experience in this study abroad. Every single day was very fulfilling, and I spent such condensed days that I almost forgot about Japan.

Korea University is one of the three major universities in Korea. It has three large hospitals within Korea, and one of them, Asan Medical Center, is ranked 30th in the world and 1st in Korea. The campus consists of buildings with character surrounded by trees, and is so vast that it is hard to believe it is in central Seoul. The hospital was also very large, a beautiful glass-walled building. Construction of a new ward building is still in progress. The level of the students was also very high compared with Japan, and I felt their abundance of knowledge and experience and was stimulated every day.

First, as for the clerkships, I did the first two weeks in breast and endocrine surgery and the last two weeks in pulmonology. On the first day of attendance I was nervous wondering what it would be like, but while waiting for the doctor, I happened to meet Lara (an exchange student from Germany) who was scheduled to rotate through the same department as me. She was very friendly, and we hit it off immediately and I was able to relax. The doctors in breast and endocrine surgery were also all cheerful and friendly. Among them, Professor Kim is a world-famous thyroid surgeon, and I was overwhelmed by both his skill and his character. He is a doctor who was formerly a professor at Johns Hopkins University, and a TV crew was there filming throughout my clerkship. Doctors and patients gathered to him from all over the world. In particular, observing the operation that the professor developed left the greatest impression. It is Transoral Robotic Thyroidectomy (TORT), and the approach to the tumor was groundbreaking and, moreover, it was a method that leaves hardly any scar after surgery. In Korea, because of insurance, many robotic operations are performed and the number of TORT cases was also large, which was very stimulating. In this unit I scrubbed into the surgical field many times and assisted in operations. I was often told "you can do it," and gained much experience such as suturing and ligation. I was also taken to a facility where one can practice with the da Vinci, and could experience everything from setting up and starting it up to mock surgery. I feel I was really lucky to meet and be taught by a wonderful doctor like Professor Kim. The doctors in pulmonology were also all very caring. Korea University Hospital is one of the very large hospitals in Korea, so the number of bronchoscopies was very high, about ten a day on busy days. Actually experiencing pulmonary function tests and prick tests myself was also a good experience. Going along on the doctors' breaks, having coffee together at the cafe and eating lunch, and chatting a lot is also a good memory.

After the clerkships I played with Lara late into the night every day. Looking back, in the three and a half weeks from the day we hit it off on the first day until she returned home, there was not a single day, holidays included, that we did not play together. She was also active, so the things we wanted to do and our conversation matched, and although our nationalities differed we enjoyed ourselves without feeling any need for reserve. The day we parted was truly sad, and we met one last time and talked a lot. During the pulmonology clerkship I met clinical clerkship students and did the clerkship with them. There my circle of friends widened again, and we played a lot after clerkships and on holidays. With one girl I was able to go out wearing hanbok together. I am still in contact with everyone I became close to during the clerkships. Thanks to everyone I had many plans every day and hardly any time alone.

Finally, about where I stayed, I did a homestay. There was no dormitory provided by the university, and since this was the first dispatch to Korea University, there was nobody to rely on and there was a lot I really did not know. As I proceeded with preparations through trial and error, I came to be in touch with a girl who attends Korea University through a chance event, and we became close. When I was consulting her about life there, she proposed that I do a homestay at her house. A homestay was my first experience, and it was also the first for her family, so both sides were unaccustomed, but I thought there could be no better opportunity and decided immediately. This became the trigger for my studying Korean too. Because we were able to meet her family beforehand over Zoom, we each had a little image of the other before I went to Korea. At first I was anxious, but when I went to Korea and actually met them, they were an extremely good family, and I immediately thought it would be fine. Especially with the mother, I spent the most time. The mother was a nurse at the hospital where I did my clerkships, and we saw each other off every day. The breakfast she always made was truly delicious and I looked forward to it. They had a cute cat at home, and when the mother was busy I was in charge of feeding it and cleaning the litter box. She also knew I like exercise and often invited me for walks. I liked the mother's personality very much, and we went hiking together on a holiday, but more than that, on weekday evenings we often walked while talking for two or three hours. Listening to the stories of the mother, who is hardworking and has a pure heart, was a time that made me feel positive too. As for my best memory with the family, it was that on the Saturday of the last week of the homestay, we all drove out together, climbed a mountain of about 1,100 m, and ate Korean food at a mountain lodge. Thanks to everyone in the host family treating me like a real family member without reserve, I was comfortable and could spend each day naturally. There are so many memories that I cannot write them all here, but each day I spent in Korea was special, and I feel as if I have gained a new family.

Having met wonderful doctors, a wonderful university, friends and family, I gained more than I could have imagined before studying abroad. I cannot express it well in words, but I surely grew and a new door opened.
I sincerely thank everyone I met and who supported me in this study abroad.
